rounds.position: A third of our healthcare and construction shift staff live in Johor, and on Wednesday they will not be able to reach work. We propose they remain in Singapore for the duration, screened on entry and tested, with employers housing them. Cargo must keep moving on the same terms as before — our fresh food arrives by road and there is no second route.

The Movement Control Order is a nationwide instrument and we will not carve an exemption out of it for one border. Our position is that the crossing closes. Whatever is agreed, Malaysians who end up on the wrong side of it must be housed and supported, and that cost cannot fall on them or on us; and our own food supply is secured before it is exported.

We hear that the objection is to daily movement rather than to the workers themselves, and an arrangement where they stay put creates no daily crossings at all — it does what your order is for. We will carry part of the accommodation cost rather than leave it with employers. Cargo has to stay unrestricted; a food export control would hit us within days and would not help your domestic supply.
rounds.concession: Shares the accommodation cost rather than leaving it with employers.

rounds.position: That distinction is the right one. If they stay in place and do not cross daily, the order's purpose is met, and we can accept that rather than a closed border. In exchange the accommodation cost has to sit with Singapore — these are workers in your economy, housed for your continuity, and our fiscal room this quarter is committed elsewhere. We can move to prioritised essentials on cargo rather than controls.
rounds.concession: Accepts workers remaining in Singapore instead of a closed border; moves from export controls to prioritised essentials.

rounds.position: Then take the full subsidy. It is the cheapest item on this table for us and plainly the most valuable one for you, and we would rather pay than spend a week negotiating while wards go unstaffed. What it buys is cargo left unrestricted — not prioritised, unrestricted — because a queue at the Causeway is a shortage in our shops three days later.

With the subsidy settled we can leave cargo unrestricted; our concern was never the lorries, it was the people. Screening and testing on entry we have wanted throughout. On those terms this is a package we can defend at home, which the closed border never quite was — it would have stranded our own citizens without an answer.

judgments.summary: Quantifies the staffing exposure precisely and names the single-route dependency, but asks the other side to absorb every cost and does not engage the purpose of the order it wants an exemption from.
States the sovereignty objection clearly and raises the welfare of its own citizens, but treats closure as the only instrument that serves the order's purpose.

unaddressed: Whether the order's aim is to stop movement or to stop the people moving
Who bears the cost if workers are stranded on either side

judgments.summary: Separates daily movement from the workers themselves, which reframes the dispute and answers the objection rather than restating the request; still argues cargo on assertion.
Accepts the reframing and prices its own concession honestly, naming fiscal commitment rather than invoking sovereignty a second time.

unaddressed: Whether prioritised essentials is materially different from unrestricted cargo at this volume

judgments.summary: Prices its own concession explicitly as cheap to itself and valuable to the other side — the argument that closes the gap — and ties the cargo ask to a concrete three-day consequence.
Concedes the issue it weights least once the one it weights most is secured, and states plainly why the closed border was worse for its own position.

recommendation.rationale: The judge's assessments converge on one exchange: the accommodation subsidy Singapore weights least is what Malaysia weights most, and Malaysia's objection was to daily crossings rather than to the workers — so an arrangement where they stay in place serves the order's purpose and Singapore's continuity at once.

options.condition: Malaysia holds that no exemption can be made to the order
options.action: frame the arrangement as ending daily crossings rather than exempting them

options.condition: Treasury resists funding accommodation in full
options.action: tie disbursement to verified headcount in essential sectors rather than reducing the amount

options.condition: Johor pushes for export controls on food
options.action: offer a standing supply review in exchange for cargo staying unrestricted

baseline.rationale: Without the other side's constraints the defensible play is to seek an exemption for cross-border workers and concede little else.

options.action: escalate to the bilateral ministerial channel
